summary: Restored tickets.sql into helpdesk, repaired PostgreSQL ID allocation, preserved all imported data and the source export, and verified persistence through a node restart.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL 10 AppStream PostgreSQL 16.15 without changing the OS release or kernel.
Initialized and enabled PostgreSQL with SELinux remaining enforcing.
Created helpdesk and restored the export transactionally.
Synchronized tickets_id_seq with the imported maximum ID.
Verified ID-less inserts allocated IDs 101 and, after restart, 102; both test transactions were rolled back.
Restarted node1 once and confirmed its boot identity changed and PostgreSQL recovered.

evidence.requirement: Restore the supplied export while preserving ticket IDs and text
evidence.summary: The database contains exactly IDs 1, 2, and 100 with subjects Printer queue, Scanner cable, and Office move.

evidence.requirement: New tickets without explicit IDs receive unique IDs above the imported maximum
evidence.summary: Transactional inserts allocated IDs 101 before restart and 102 afterward; the original dataset retained three distinct IDs.
The source remains at the required path with unchanged SHA-256 5a9b51de0c539f9ffedd0ca1424be6549bbef62a5414b6545d879d9c1be973c5, metadata, and contents.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were retained; PostgreSQL 16.15 came from the native RHEL AppStream repository. SELinux remains enforcing.

Healthy baseline boot ID 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9 was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID d76eff3f-012a-4e03-9254-c0b2aaa0a08d observed, and PostgreSQL plus database contents and sequence behavior recovered.
